title: What is known about 1RB0RE_1RC0RE_1LD1RB_1LA0LA_1RF0LC_---0RC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RE_1RC0RE_1LD1RB_1LA0LA_1RF0LC_---0RC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state machine halts from blank tape. This page describes what its run looks like at the level of words and counters, what a halt would need, and what is still missing. The description comes from simulation (first look, about an hour of study); nothing beyond the bounded runs is proved.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 107 steps, the C simulator none in 109. The macro structure described below is observed in the simulation, not proved.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 317,889 cells have been visited and 200,524 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/linear
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows in proportion to the step count (the head drifts steadily that way) (fitted exponent 1.248). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: Two encodings
claims.text: Blocks 1, 1^2, 1^3 when the head is at the left end, 1^3, 1^7, 1^12, ... when it is at the right end: apparently the same list in two encodings (observed).

claims.title: Shift rules, for every n
claims.text: B crosses (01)^n to the right and leaves (11)^n; C crosses (10)^n and leaves (11)^n.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. No macro rule has been proved for this machine yet; see the README's Later section for the next steps.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. The head carries a string of digits across the tape, rewriting it between a short and a long encoding on each sweep, and keeps coming back to the left end, which grows.

facts.text: the tape grows to the left about like t^0.7
No halt in the C simulator; 317,889 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: Digits in two encodings
html: The tape is a string of short blocks of 1s separated by single 0s. When the head is at the left end, the blocks are 1, 1^2, 1^3 (step 93,167,380: A>0 1^2 0 1^2 0 1^2 0 1 0 1 0 1^2 0 …); when it has reached the right end, the blocks are longer, 1^3, 1^7, 1^10, 1^12, 1^16 (step 25,763,983, from the left: 1^2 0 1^12 0 1^12 0 1 0 1^3 0 1^12 0 1 0 1^7 0 …). As in the G13 family of 1RB0LA_1RC---_0LD1RD_0RA0RE_0RF1RC_1LF0LA, the head seems to carry one list of numbers across the tape, rewriting it between two encodings.
The head returns to the left end in state A often (30,210 times in the first 108 steps) and the tape grows to the left: 3,000 cells at 3.6·106 steps, 30,000 at 9.3·107.

sections.heading: What a halt would need
html: The machine halts when it reads a 0 in state F (F0 is the halting transition). F is entered from E on a 0 (E0 = 1RF), so a halt needs E>0 0.

sections.heading: Shift rules
html: Two shift rules are proved for every length: B over (01)^n and C over (10)^n, each leaving (11)^n. They are the pieces of the rightward encoding. The exact correspondence between the two encodings was not found.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows in proportion to the step count (the head drifts steadily that way) (fitted exponent 1.248). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 317,889 cells (165,431 left of the start, 5,264 right), with a density of 1s of 0.631.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: digit string in two encodings, swept from the left end
summary: The tape is a string of short blocks of 1s whose lengths are digits, written one way (1, 1^2, 1^3) when the head is at the left end and another way (1^3, 1^7, 1^12, ...) when it is at the right end; the head keeps returning to the growing left end.
